source_caption:
Imagine shutting down the "Center of the World" for 3 hours just to film a nightmare.

In 2000, director Cameron Crowe achieved the impossible for his psychological thriller, Vanilla Sky. He convinced the NYPD to block off 20 blocks of Times Square on a Sunday morning. The scene was filmed in Times Square, New York City. The production team paidIn 2000, director Cameron Crowe achieved the impossible for his psychological thriller, Vanilla Sky over $1 million to secure the permits and logistical support needed to shut down 20 blocks of Times Square for three hours. The shutdown lasted for 3 hours (5 AM to 8 AM on a Sunday), and was filmed without CGI, relying instead on practical, real-life, and costly logistical efforts. Making it one of the most expensive and surreal scenes in film history.

source_details.title: Vanilla Sky
source_details.synopsis: Vanilla Sky is a 2001 American science fiction psychological thriller film starring Tom Cruise as a magazine publisher who begins to question reality after being disfigured in a car crash. Written and directed by Cameron Crowe, who also produced with Cruise and Paula Wagner, it is an English-language remake of the 1997 Spanish film Open Your Eyes, which was written by Alejandro Amenábar and Mateo Gil. The supporting cast includes Penélope Cruz (who reprises her role from the original), Kurt Russell, Jason Lee, Noah Taylor, and Cameron Diaz.
